newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: The Swiss franc's rise to its highest levels versus the mark in over seven months boosted prices of short-dated Swiss franc debt, while bond prices fell.

The three-month EuroSwiss contract traded on LIFFE ended up six basis points at 98.25, as the Swiss franc surged. The market may be speculating that a prolongued Swiss franc rise will encourage the Swiss National Bank to keep its monetary policy generous.
At the same time, prices of longer-dated paper were weaker, with the Swiss market looking to a Swiss federal government bond auction next week.
Commenting on the day's activity, one Swiss-based trader said that the market saw a poor performance in Switzerland.

But he added that traders who were short the market in 2006, 2007, 2008 maturities may be looking to cover. Those maturities were likely to be the main focus of the new Swiss federal government auction on Thursday, May 22.

At the same time, the market was under pressure due to expectations for an offering by Swiss Cantons next week, expected only a day or two before the government tender. The market already has seen a slew of new issues in the past week.
Swiss trade will be closed Monday for Whit Monday.
Euro Swiss francs up six at 98.25.
